exposure: Severe maternal morbidity (SMM) status (no SMM, any SMM, SMM excluding cases with blood transfusion as the only indicator)
Patient characteristics (age, race/ethnicity, primary payer, income)
outcome: Incidence rates of any SMM and SMM excluding blood transfusion as the only indicator
cohort: The cohort included all delivery hospitalizations identified from the National Inpatient Sample dataset between 2014 and 2019.
finding: Deliveries affected by severe maternal morbidity incur significantly higher hospitalization costs compared to those without SMM, and these costs generally increased annually from 2014 to 2019, with disparities observed across patient, delivery method, and hospital characteristics.
mod_finding: Hospitalization costs for SMM were higher for cesarean deliveries.
